summary: Executable files exclude writers until the last image ends, and bind mounts keep removed files of the KRFFS boot root until the last holder ends, each program on a boot of its own of the x86-64 test image

cases.behavior: an executable file refuses writers and truncation while an image of it runs, and takes them again once the last image has ended, on the KRFFS boot root and on a tmpfs

execution.cleanup: the copies, the tmpfs and its directory under /tmp, which the program removes on every exit, and its workspace

assertions.checks: while two copies of the program run from a scratch directory of the KRFFS boot root, opens of the file for writing, reading and writing, and with O_TRUNC, and truncate(2), are each ETXTBSY, through a new name after a rename and, on tmpfs, through a hard link; a read-only descriptor's ftruncate is EINVAL and fallocate EBADF; an exec is ETXTBSY while a duplicate of a writer is open; once the last image ends, by exit or by exec of another program, the file can be written and truncated again, also after a forked image; an image runs on after its file is unlinked; a failed exec of a file that is no program leaves it writable; and an ELF interpreter is held like the program that names it, through a rename and an unlink

while two copies of the program run from a tmpfs mounted in the workspace, opens of the file for writing, reading and writing, and with O_TRUNC, and truncate(2), are each ETXTBSY, through a new name after a rename and, on tmpfs, through a hard link; a read-only descriptor's ftruncate is EINVAL and fallocate EBADF; an exec is ETXTBSY while a duplicate of a writer is open; once the last image ends, by exit or by exec of another program, the file can be written and truncated again, also after a forked image; an image runs on after its file is unlinked; a failed exec of a file that is no program leaves it writable; and an ELF interpreter is held like the program that names it, through a rename and an unlink

cases.behavior: a file of the KRFFS boot root held through a bind mount of its directory keeps its bytes after it loses its name, through the original or through the bind, and returns its blocks when its last holder ends

execution.cleanup: the bind mount and its directory under /tmp, which the program removes on every exit, and its workspace

assertions.checks: the read-only bind refuses to remove the name with EROFS, and with the file unlinked through the original directory: a descriptor and its duplicate keep the file's bytes, the first close keeps its blocks and the last returns them; its bytes outlast a new file written after the name goes, and the free blocks come back to their count before the row

the read-only bind refuses to remove the name with EROFS, and with the file renamed over through the original directory: a descriptor and its duplicate keep the file's bytes, the first close keeps its blocks and the last returns them; its bytes outlast a new file written after the name goes, and the free blocks come back to their count before the row

the read-only bind refuses to remove the name with EROFS, and with the file unlinked through the original directory: a private mapping made through the bind keeps the file's bytes after its descriptor closes, and munmap returns its blocks; its bytes outlast a new file written after the name goes, and the free blocks come back to their count before the row
